problem: Prior VLN agents in the panoramic action space represent each navigable candidate by the single view it lies in. Instructions often cite landmarks outside that view as references (e.g., 'the archway to the left of the mirror'), so textual-visual matching fails when several similar candidates exist.
motivation: Referenced landmarks frequently sit in views adjacent to a candidate. Naively fusing neighbor views adds unmentioned clutter, such as a lamp, and some instructions ('go through the doorway') need no context at all. The paper therefore splits instructions into action, subject and reference phrases, and fuses neighbor-view context adaptively and selectively.
key_idea: Enrich each navigation candidate with context from its neighbor views through three modules scored separately and combined with phrase-conditioned weights: a subject module (global view features weighted by spatial affinity), a reference module (neighbor objects attended by reference phrases) and an action module (orientation).
insight: Neighbor-view context helps over single-view candidates. With the reference module removed, a subject module that fuses 4 neighbor views by orientation affinity reaches 57.9 SR / 53.9 SPL on R2R val-unseen, versus 55.6 / 50.7 for a single-view subject (Table 4). Fusing by spatial affinity beats fusing with language as the query (56.4 / 52.2), which the authors attribute to the language-vision embedding gap. The module ablation (Table 3) shows the action/orientation module matters most (removing it: 60.1→48.6 SR, 54.9→44.0 SPL) and the subject module second (50.4 / 44.6), while the reference module adds only ~1 SPL, partly because references are already captured in the global neighbor views. More context is not always better: 8 neighbors or 4/12 objects per view underperform 4 neighbors × 8 objects (Table 5), because redundant views and objects dilute attention.
method: EnvDrop baseline: Bi-LSTM instruction encoder, LSTM decoder with soft attention over 36 panoramic views; view feature = ResNet-152 (Places365) + orientation embedding (cos/sin of heading and elevation repeated 32×).

Phrase extractor: three independent soft-attentions over the instruction, conditioned on the previous state, produce action/subject/reference phrase features u_a, u_s, u_r and specialized context states h̃_a, h̃_s, h̃_r (separate linear projections); the global state is their average.

Subject module: projects ResNet features of each candidate's 4 neighbor views and aggregates them with scaled dot-product attention whose query is the candidate orientation and keys are the neighbor orientations (spatial affinity). Confidence τ_s = h̃_sᵀ W̃_s F^s.

Reference module: takes the top-8 Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome) object labels per neighbor view, restricted to the 100 most frequent R2R classes and GloVe-encoded, concatenated with each object's orientation relative to the candidate (approximated by its view orientation). These 32 objects are attended with u_r as query to form F^r; confidence τ_r = h̃_rᵀ W̃_r F^r.
Action module (following OAAM): projects the candidate's orientation embedding and scores it against the action state h̃_a to get τ_a.
Adaptive action integrator: softmax-normalized weights w_a, w_s, w_r computed from linear projections of u_a, u_s, u_r; final candidate probability = softmax_k(w_a τ_a + w_s τ_s + w_r τ_r).

Training: IL + RL (A2C) with goal and fidelity rewards. Two stages on R2R: 80k iterations on real data, then real plus Speaker-Follower synthetic data up to 200k iterations. R4R uses stage 1 only. RMSprop, lr 1e-4, D_k = 512.

setting.backbone: EnvDrop-style Bi-LSTM encoder + LSTM decoder with attention modules (trained from scratch) on frozen ResNet-152 (Places365) view features and Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome) object labels embedded with GloVe
setting.training_data: R2R: R2R train, then additionally Speaker-Follower synthetic augmented instruction-trajectory data (two-stage EnvDrop training). R4R: R4R train only (stage 1, no synthetic data). No large-scale pre-training.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 discrete views, precomputed ResNet features) + object detections in neighbor views + view orientations
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic action space, select a navigable candidate)

numbers_note: The paper prints SR/SPL/CLS/nDTW/sDTW as fractions (e.g., 0.60); these are converted to 0-100 here. Ablation Tables 3-5 report the full model on R2R with three decimals (val seen 0.686 SR / 0.645 SPL; val unseen 0.601 SR / 0.549 SPL); ablated variants are not listed as separate entries.
results: On R2R, NvEM reaches 60 SR / 55 SPL on val-unseen and 58 SR / 54 SPL on test. That is +7 SPL over its EnvDrop baseline (48/47 SPL) and about +2 over the prior non-pretrained SOTA RelGraph (57/53 and 55/52). It also beats pre-trained PRESS, PREVALENT and VLNBert (init. OSCAR), but not VLNBert initialized from PREVALENT (63 SR / 57 SPL test). On R4R val-unseen it sets a new SOTA with 38 SR / 28 SPL / 41 CLS / 36 nDTW / 20 sDTW, versus reimplemented RelGraph at 35 / 25 / 37 / 32 / 18.
limitations: Phrase decomposition relies on unsupervised soft attention and is sometimes wrong; the failure case shows the subject module attending to the wrong phrase ('bathroom').

Object positions are coarsely approximated by their view orientation, and the neighborhood is fixed (4 views × 8 objects); more neighbors or objects hurt performance, so context selection remains brittle.
Evaluated only on discrete-graph R2R/R4R with an LSTM backbone; it still trails in-domain pre-trained VLN-BERT (PREVALENT init.), and extensions to continuous or dialog VLN are left to future work.
